Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Wall Street sees the Treasury market emerging as a winner from the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections, giving traders another reason to rethink this year’s sharp selloff.
The party’s sweep of Congress was seized upon by bond bulls after tech stocks tumbled on speculation the political shift will tap the brakes on an artificial-intelligence investment boom that’s been fueling economic growth, fanning inflation and pushing up interest rates as companies flood the market with debt to finance it.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A Houthi attack damaged one of the landmarks of the Saudi Arabian capital’s financial district, upsetting plans for a return to normal about a month after deadly strikes on Riyadh’s airport disrupted travel and canceled showpiece events.
The offices of state oil giant Saudi Aramco suffered minor damage as the city fended off a new barrage of ballistic and cruise missiles on Sunday. There were no deaths or injuries, the state-run Saudi Press Agency reported.

item.title: Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
item.description:
Wall Street Week • Nov 8th, 2026
Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
Europe’s postwar welfare state was built for a younger, growing population. Today, aging communities are putting pensions, health care and public finances under mounting strain. As governments try to fund defense, infrastructure and education at the same time, the fight over who pays is spilling into politics and the streets.

item.title: Seattle and Las Vegas Make Their NBA Pitch
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg senior sports reporter Randall Williams explains why the NBA’s potential expansion to Seattle and Las Vegas could generate billions of dollars while raising questions about the financial returns for existing owners. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Williams also examines the competition among prospective ownership groups, LIV Golf’s struggles and the labor battle threatening Major League Baseball’s next season. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Peace Push Returns to Abu Dhabi
item.description: US, Ukrainian and Russian delegations are scheduled to meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10th and 11th, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to represent the US. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend former Deputy Secretary of State Stephen Biegun discusses how a Democratic-controlled Congress could bring greater scrutiny to President Donald Trump’s foreign policy as the US renews efforts to negotiate an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
item.description: President Donald Trump’s return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies’ desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock.

item.title: Democratic Sweep Tests Trump-Linked Trades Across Latin America
item.description: Investors who spent the past year factoring countries’ standing with Donald Trump into their Latin America trades are confronting a new variable: a Democratic-controlled US Congress.

item.title: How Everyday Apps Feed Police Surveillance
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg investigative journalist Ryan Gallagher explains how location data collected through everyday smartphone apps can ultimately be sold to law enforcement agencies, often without users knowing where their information ends up. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gallagher details how Penlink’s surveillance technology can track phones using commercially obtained data and why its use has fueled calls for greater privacy protections and oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)
